name: real-time-collaborative-editing

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: The WebSocket $connect route handler does not implement authentication checks. Any client can establish a connection and begin sending/receiving updates.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker can connect to the WebSocket API endpoint without authentication and potentially access or modify collaborative documents.

recommendations.description: Implement AWS IAM authentication for WebSocket connections
recommendations.implementationDetails: Use IAM authorizer with the WebSocket API and require signed requests using AWS SigV4. Update the CDK code to add authorization:

recommendations.description: Implement connection validation in the $connect route
recommendations.implementationDetails: Add authentication and authorization checks in the sync-handler.ts $connect route before allowing connections

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Consider using Amazon Cognito for user authentication and AWS WAF for additional API protection. Implement proper IAM roles and policies for the API Gateway and Lambda integration.

ground_truth.threatName: Insufficient Access Control for Document Operations

mitreATT&CK: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: The current implementation lacks document-level access control checks in the sync-handler.ts and state-handler.ts Lambda functions. DynamoDB and S3 access is controlled only at the service level, not the document level.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An authenticated user could modify their requests to access or modify documents owned by other users by manipulating document IDs or connection parameters.

recommendations.implementationDetails: Add an access control table in DynamoDB to store document permissions. Modify Lambda functions to check permissions before any document operations.

recommendations.description: Implement S3 bucket policies for attachments
recommendations.implementationDetails: Use S3 bucket policies and object-level permissions to restrict access to attachments based on document ownership and sharing settings.

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Use IAM policy conditions to enforce fine-grained access control. Consider implementing AWS Organizations SCPs for additional security boundaries.

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: The APIs lack proper rate limiting and connection throttling. A single client can establish multiple connections or send numerous requests, potentially exhausting system resources.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker could create multiple WebSocket connections or GraphQL subscriptions, overwhelming the system's capacity to handle legitimate requests.

recommendations.description: Implement AWS WAF with rate limiting
recommendations.implementationDetails: Add AWS WAF to the API Gateway and AppSync APIs with rate limiting rules and IP-based restrictions
Add connection tracking in DynamoDB and implement limits per user/IP in the sync-handler.ts $connect route

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Use AWS Shield for additional DDoS protection. Consider implementing AWS WAF rate-based rules and AWS Shield Advanced for critical workloads.

mitreATT&CK: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: While the CDK code shows encryption enabled for some services, it uses AWS managed keys instead of customer managed keys (CMK) from KMS, potentially limiting control over key rotation and access.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker with access to the storage layer could potentially access sensitive document data if encryption is compromised or improperly configured.

recommendations.description: Implement KMS encryption for all storage services
recommendations.implementationDetails: Use customer managed KMS keys for DynamoDB tables, S3 bucket, and ElastiCache cluster encryption
Ensure all communication between services uses TLS 1.2 or higher, implement proper SSL/TLS configuration for ElastiCache

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Use AWS KMS with automatic key rotation. Consider using AWS Secrets Manager for managing encryption keys and other secrets.

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: The Lambda functions process JSON data from WebSocket messages and GraphQL operations without proper validation or sanitization, potentially allowing injection of malicious content.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker could send specially crafted JSON payloads that exploit parsing vulnerabilities or inject malicious content into stored documents.

recommendations.implementationDetails: Add JSON schema validation for WebSocket messages and GraphQL operations in Lambda functions
Configure AWS WAF with rules to detect and block common injection patterns

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Use AWS WAF managed rules for common vulnerabilities. Consider implementing AWS Lambda function URLs with additional security controls.

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: The conflict resolution system may fail to properly handle race conditions or concurrent updates, potentially leading to lost updates or inconsistent document state.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: Multiple users making simultaneous updates could trigger race conditions that the conflict resolution system fails to handle, resulting in data loss or corruption.

recommendations.implementationDetails: Implement proper Operational Transformation (OT) or Conflict-free Replicated Data Types (CRDT) in the conflict-handler.ts Lambda function
Add proper error handling, retries, and monitoring for the SQS queue and conflict resolution process

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Use AWS X-Ray for distributed tracing. Implement proper CloudWatch alarms and metrics for monitoring the conflict resolution system.

#!/usr/bin/env python3

# AWS Service Category Imports
# Network and Content Delivery
from diagrams import Diagram, Cluster, Edge
from diagrams.aws.network import APIGateway
from diagrams.aws.mobile import APIGatewayEndpoint

# Application Integration
from diagrams.aws.integration import Appsync, SimpleQueueServiceSqsQueue as SQS

# Database and Storage
from diagrams.aws.database import Dynamodb, ElastiCache
from diagrams.aws.storage import S3

# Compute
from diagrams.aws.compute import Lambda

# Graph attributes for better visualization
graph_attr = {
    "fontsize": "45",
    "bgcolor": "white",
    "splines": "spline",
    "pad": "1.0",
    "nodesep": "0.75",
    "ranksep": "1.0",
    "fontname": "Arial"
}

# Edge labels with detailed descriptions
edge_labels = {
    "websocket_connect": "WebSocket /connect",
    "websocket_message": "WebSocket /message",
    "realtime_sync": "Process Updates",
    "state_sync": "Sync Document State",
    "conflict_check": "Check for Conflicts",
    "store_version": "Store New Version",
    "broadcast_ws": "Broadcast via WebSocket",
    "broadcast_gql": "Broadcast via GraphQL Subscription"
}

# Create the diagram with custom attributes
with Diagram(
    "Real-time Collaborative Editing Platform",
    filename="data/real-time-collaborative-editing/architecture",
    show=False,
    direction="LR",
    graph_attr=graph_attr
):
    # Define edge attributes for better visibility
    normal_edge = Edge(color="black", fontname="Arial")
    highlight_edge = Edge(color="darkgreen", style="bold", fontname="Arial")
    bidirectional = Edge(color="darkblue", style="bold", dir="both", fontname="Arial")

    # Client Users Cluster
    with Cluster("Collaborative Users"):
        users = [
            APIGatewayEndpoint("User 1\nWeb Client"),
            APIGatewayEndpoint("User 2\nMobile Client"),
            APIGatewayEndpoint("User N\nDesktop Client")
        ]

    # Real-time Sync Cluster
    with Cluster("Real-time Communication Layer"):
        api_gateway = APIGateway("WebSocket API\nReal-time Updates")
        appsync = Appsync("GraphQL API\nSubscriptions")
        sync_lambda = Lambda("Sync Handler\nCollaboration Logic")

    # Data Storage Cluster
    with Cluster("Data Management"):
        # Document Storage and Versioning
        with Cluster("Document Storage"):
            dynamodb_docs = Dynamodb("Documents")
            dynamodb_versions = Dynamodb("Versions")
            s3_attachments = S3("Attachments")

        # Real-time State Management
        with Cluster("State Management"):
            cache = ElastiCache("Real-time State")
            state_lambda = Lambda("State Handler")

    # Conflict Resolution Cluster
    with Cluster("Conflict Resolution"):
        conflict_lambda = Lambda("Resolution Handler\nOT/CRDT Logic")
        conflict_queue = SQS("Conflict Queue")

    # Connect Users to Communication Layer
    for user in users:
        user >> Edge(color="darkgreen", style="bold", label=edge_labels["websocket_connect"]) >> api_gateway
        user >> Edge(color="darkblue", style="bold", dir="both", label=edge_labels["websocket_message"]) >> api_gateway
        user - Edge(color="darkgreen", style="dashed", label="Subscribe") - appsync

    # Real-time Sync Flow with Labels
    api_gateway >> Edge(color="darkgreen", label=edge_labels["realtime_sync"]) >> sync_lambda
    
    # Data Flow with Labels
    sync_lambda - Edge(color="darkblue", style="bold", dir="both", label=edge_labels["state_sync"]) - dynamodb_docs
    sync_lambda >> Edge(label=edge_labels["store_version"]) >> dynamodb_versions
    sync_lambda >> Edge(label="Store Attachments") >> s3_attachments
    
    # State Management Flow
    sync_lambda >> Edge(label="Update State") >> state_lambda >> cache
    cache - Edge(color="darkblue", style="bold", dir="both", label="Cache Sync") - state_lambda
    
    # Conflict Resolution Flow
    sync_lambda >> Edge(label=edge_labels["conflict_check"]) >> conflict_queue >> conflict_lambda
    
    # Bidirectional Sync with Labels
    conflict_lambda - Edge(color="darkblue", style="bold", dir="both", label="Resolve Conflicts") - dynamodb_docs
    conflict_lambda - Edge(color="darkblue", style="bold", dir="both", label="Update State") - cache
    
    # Broadcast Updates
    state_lambda >> Edge(label=edge_labels["broadcast_ws"]) >> api_gateway
    state_lambda >> Edge(label=edge_labels["broadcast_gql"]) >> appsync
